title: Headroom off-by-one + epoch race causing silent reserved-capacity shortfalls: hotfix, customer remediation, and follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers observed elevated 429/503 errors during short multi-minute traffic bursts despite available reserved pool headroom. Root cause traced to a headroom calculation bug introduced alongside an epoch-boundary ledger update optimization. The combination produced an off-by-one reserve undercount and, in a small percentage of allocator cycles (~0.7%), removed safety headroom causing silent capacity shortfalls for medium-sized tenants during burst windows.
steps_taken: 2025-02-18 09:12 - Alert from CS: OrbitalHealth reporting 30% increased 429s across two regions during morning surge; assigned ENG-681422.
2025-02-18 09:40 - Triage call with oncall, allocator team, and SEs; initial mitigation plan: temporarily raise global headroom multiplier to 1.15 to avoid immediate customer impact.
2025-02-18 10:10 - Deployed temporary config bump (config: global_headroom_multiplier=1.15) to eu-west and us-central via runtime-config; 10-minute observation window.
2025-02-18 10:30 - Observed reduced 429 spike for reporting tenants; initiated in-depth telemetry correlation.
2025-02-18 11:00 - Collected allocator traces, ledger updates, and headroom estimator logs for impacted tenants for the prior 6 hours.
2025-02-18 13:25 - Reproduced underload in staging with synthetic burst script (tenant-sim v2) by creating epoch boundary condition and concurrent ledger flush.
2025-02-18 16:40 - Implemented and tested patch to fix integer rounding/off-by-one and added lock around epoch transition to prevent race with ledger flush.
2025-02-19 02:15 - Hotfix PR prepared, reviewed, and merged (see linked_prs).
2025-02-19 03:30 - Gradual canary rollout to 3 AZs, monitor headroom telemetry and 429 rate for 60 minutes, then full rollout across dedicated clusters.
2025-02-20 15:00 - Final validation with OrbitalHealth and customer SLA owners; issue marked mitigated and communications sent.
telemetry_findings: Headroom estimator returned an integer floor during byte-to-slot conversion which produced off-by-one reserves for sequences near threshold.
Epoch-flush path could update tenant_ledger asynchronously without synchronizing with compute_headroom(), allowing a window where ledger reflected more free tokens than were actually redeemable.
Affected tenant patterns: medium bursty tenants with 2-6 concurrent requests and sequence lengths above the 95th percentile for their profile.
Incidence rate in production: ~0.7% of allocator cycles across dedicated pools during high churn windows; correlated strongly with rolling upgrade windows and high ledger flush frequency.
root_cause: A two-factor failure: (1) an off-by-one truncation in the headroom conversion (integer division when computing slots from bytes) and (2) an epoch-boundary race where the ledger flush occurred concurrently with headroom computation, enabling the allocator to believe an extra slot was available. Together these reduced effective reserved headroom below the safety margin, allowing bursts to exhaust capacity silently.

rollout_notes: Canary rollout: 3 AZs (eu-west-1a, us-central-1b, us-east-1c) for 60m monitoring headroom_gauge, 429-rate, and allocator_rejects metric.
Full rollout completed 2025-02-19 05:10 UTC across dedicated clusters with no regression signals.
Rollback plan: revert merge and reapply temporary global_headroom_multiplier=1.2 if regressions appear during rollout.
Post-deploy: monitor for 72 hours on canary and full clusters; increase retention for allocator traces for impacted tenants to 14 days.
customer_comms: 2025-02-18 12:00 - Initial acknowledgement to OrbitalHealth and affected tenants, we are investigating and applied temporary headroom increase.
2025-02-19 06:00 - Update: root cause identified; hotfix deployed and validated; recommended action for tenants: none required.
follow_up_actions: Add unit tests to cover byte->slot rounding boundaries (done in PR).
Add integration test in CI that reproduces epoch-boundary ledger flush + headroom compute race (in progress, estimate 3).
Add a telemetry alert for headroom_delta < -2 within a single allocator cycle and a runbook to auto-increase global headroom for affected pools.
Document the ledger/epoch contract in Confluence and require design review for any future ledger optimizations.
Postmortem write-up and customer RCA to be posted to Confluence and shared with impacted customers by 2025-03-05.
